headline_marked: State Minister Humaiun Kobir: [[Bangladesh not invited to BRICS Summit]]
headline: State Minister Humaiun Kobir: Bangladesh not invited to BRICS Summit
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was not invited to the upcoming BRICS Summit, according to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir. Bangladesh's participation hinges on its role as BIMSTEC Chair.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated today that Bangladesh has no scope to join the BRICS Summit as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was not invited. The invitation was extended to the BIMSTEC Chair, not directly to the Prime Minister.
"How shall we go? Has anyone from the Bangladesh government been invited? Our prime minister was not invited," Kobir told reporters, clarifying that the BIMSTEC Chair received the invitation.
Kobir also mentioned that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's first visit to India will be a bilateral one, not multilateral. The government is working to arrange this visit when the timing is suitable.

Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of BIMSTEC in April last year for a two-year term, underscoring its commitment to regional cooperation. BIMSTEC comprises seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.

India, which confirmed extending an invitation to the Prime Minister as BIMSTEC Chair, has a separate bilateral invitation in place since February. The 18th BRICS Summit is scheduled for September 12-13 in New Delhi, India.

headline_marked: Chattogram sees [[585 dengue cases]] in first nine days of September
headline: Chattogram sees 585 dengue cases in first nine days of September
summary: Dengue cases in Chattogram have nearly doubled in the first nine days of September compared to August, straining local hospitals and causing financial hardship for families.
details: Chattogram recorded 585 dengue cases in the first nine days of September, a significant increase from the 1,202 cases reported throughout August. This surge is attributed to intermittent rains creating ideal breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes.

The district has reported a total of 2,621 dengue cases and six deaths this year. Cases have risen sharply since July, with August seeing more than double the number of infections from the previous month.

Local health facilities are struggling to cope with the influx of patients. Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH) has 71 patients in its dedicated dengue unit, which has a capacity of only 40 beds, leading to some patients being treated on the ward floor.

The outbreak is imposing a heavy financial burden on low-income families. One patient's wife shared that her husband, a day laborer, is bedridden with dengue, halting their sole source of income and making it difficult to afford treatment and tests.

Dengue is no longer confined to urban areas, with patients now being reported from rural upazilas and hill districts. Health experts emphasize the need for early detection and dedicated hospital care.

While the fatality rate remains low at 0.22 percent this year, doctors are observing a higher proportion of severe dengue cases this month. They stress the importance of close monitoring, especially after the fever subsides.

Health officials are conducting mosquito-control drives and destroying larvae, but they urge residents to take personal responsibility by removing stagnant water around their homes and workplaces to prevent mosquito breeding.
